correctness.rationale: The unimodular first-difference map sends the anchored cycle dual Lipschitz ball bijectively to a cube conditioned on one symmetric sum inequality. The uniform increment second-moment density follows by Fourier transform from the exact uniform characteristic-function ODE; integrating gives v, while the conditioned total-square moment gives b. Exchangeability proves the rank-one increment covariance. Symmetric unimodality and a strict paired-integral inequality give eta<0 for nonredundant closing edges. Sherman–Morrison and first differences yield the tridiagonal inverse and determinant. Donsker convergence with positive-probability endpoint conditioning, Gaussian regression, and uniform integrability establish the critical Brownian law. An independent exact rational polytope triangulation verifies 18 rational cases in dimensions 2,3,4. The finite cases corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The law of a uniform point of a metric Lipschitz dual ball is a natural convex-geometric invariant. For every dimension and every real deformation parameter, one explicit spline integration evaluates every pairwise covariance and an exact banded precision operator. The terminal pinning coefficient is strictly positive precisely while the closing metric edge is effective, supplying a geometric detection of metric redundancy absent from volume alone. The sharp sqrt(d) window and non-Gaussian bridge mixture make the structural effect quantitative across dimensions. It is not an isolated small computation or a scalar volume recapitulation.
